title: [android][expo-image-picker] content:// URIs are not usable in ExponentImagePicker.launchImageLibraryAparticipant99
body: After upgrading to Expo SDK 49 with expo-image-picker ~14.3.2, some Android users can select an image in the new picker UI, but the picker promise rejects instead of returning the asset: `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Uri lacks 'file' scheme: content://media/picker/...`. It appears to affect images exposed through `content://` URIs, mainly on Android 12 and 13. I cannot reproduce it on my Android 9 test device and do not personally have a newer Android phone. Is there a workaround or a flag to restore the old picker UI?

symptoms_visible: After the Expo SDK 49 upgrade, affected Android users select a photo in the new picker UI, but launchImageLibraryAparticipant99 rejects with 'Uri lacks file scheme: content://media/picker/...' and the photo is not displayed.
N0.label: N0 content URI picker failure reported

symptoms_visible: The same image-picker rejection remains; whatwg-fetch 3.6.2 is already installed, and the reporter's error is not the fetch status-0 error addressed by that suggestion.
N1_x.label: N1_x whatwg-fetch downgrade aftermath

symptoms_visible: Sentry reports show the failure mainly on Android 12 and 13; after a user chooses a photo, the picker closes and its promise enters the catch handler, so the app never displays the selected image.
Users who had uploaded photos successfully for years began failing after the SDK 49 release.
N1.label: N1 affected versions and behavior established

symptoms_visible: The reporter reproduces the rejection on a Pixel 6 API 33 Android 13 emulator by downloading a photo in Chrome and selecting it in the new picker UI.
The error does not reproduce with the old picker UI, while the reporter's APK reproduces it on the same emulator where Expo's test app can select and display the image.
N2.label: N2 reproducible on reporter APK

symptoms_visible: Existing builds using expo-image-picker 14.5.0 still reject selected photos with the same 'Uri lacks file scheme' message on affected Android 12, 13, and 14 devices.
N3.label: N3 picker-only update insufficient

symptoms_visible: The locally produced APK still fails, but a fresh EAS-server build of the same app can select and display the image successfully on the Pixel 6 API 33 emulator.
N4.label: N4 clean-build comparison isolates stale native code

symptoms_visible: Dependency inspection shows expo-image-manipulator 11.3.0 keeping expo-image-loader 4.3.0 in affected local builds; another affected user reports that moving to expo-image-manipulator 11.5.0 makes the Android picker work.
N5.label: N5 transitive image-loader version confirmed

symptoms_visible: Fresh Android builds containing expo-image-loader 4.4.0 through aligned expo-image-picker and expo-image-manipulator versions successfully return and display photos selected through the Android picker.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved with aligned dependencies and clean native build

solution.intent: Treat the rejection as the unrelated React Native fetch regression and downgrade whatwg-fetch to 3.6.2.
solution.concrete_example: Downgrade whatwg-fetch to 3.6.2, which fixed a similar local-file fetch error.

edges.comment: Thread c1-c4: the reporter already had whatwg-fetch 3.6.2 and demonstrated that this was not the fetch status-0 error, so this direction was explicitly rejected.

question_patterns: Which Android versions and devices are affected?
Can you share the OS and device distribution from the reports?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The Sentry reports are mainly from Android 12 and 13. My Android 9 test device does not reproduce it; later reports include a Xiaomi Mi 10T Pro on Android 12 and Pixel devices on Android 13 or 14.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It only happens on the Android 9 test device and there are no reports from Android 12 or 13.
Most reports are Android 13 rather than an even split between Android 12 and 13.

question_patterns: Does the picker dismiss without returning the selected image?
Does launchImageLibraryAparticipant99 resolve or enter the catch handler?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The picker dismisses after selection, but launchImageLibraryAparticipant99 enters the catch handler. The photo-display logic is in then, so nothing appears.

question_patterns: Did these users successfully upload images before the SDK 49 upgrade?
Is this limited to new users or devices?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: One affected Android 12 user had uploaded around ten photos per week for three years. The failures started after the SDK 49 app release, and analytics showed upload starts with no successful completions.

edges.comment: Thread c7-c17 and c36-c42: device reports, promise behavior, and production history establish a modern-Android SDK 49 regression.

question_patterns: Can you reproduce this on an Android 13 emulator using your app?
Please try the affected app on a Pixel API 33 emulator and document exact steps.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I reproduced it on a Pixel 6 API 33 Android 13 emulator. I downloaded an image in Chrome, opened my app's new image picker, selected that file, and received the same rejection.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The reporter's app works on API 33 and only fails on the Android 9 device using the old picker.
The same reproduction works on a Pixel 5 API 33 emulator instead of Pixel 6.

question_patterns: Does the failure occur with both the old and new Android picker UIs?
Is the behavior specific to the modern photo picker?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It does not reproduce in emulators using the old picker UI. It reproduces in the new Android picker UI.

question_patterns: Can you share a build that reproduces the problem?
Does Expo's test app reproduce on the same emulator?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My APK reproduces consistently on the Pixel 6 API 33 emulator, but the Expo developer can download the same images and display them successfully with the test app on the same device profile.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Both the reporter APK and Expo's minimal test app fail identically on a clean API 33 emulator.

question_patterns: Are content URIs themselves unexpected or invalid here?
What URI scheme does the Android photo picker normally return?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The Android photo picker normally returns all selected photos as content URIs. expo-image-picker is expected to convert them to accessible file URIs.

edges.comment: Thread c51-c66: the reporter produced a reliable emulator reproduction and APK. The same asset and emulator worked in Expo's test app, indicating app-specific native state rather than unsupported content URIs.

question_patterns: Please install expo-image-picker 14.5.0 and test a newly submitted app version.
Does upgrading to the image-picker release containing the image-loader fix resolve the affected build?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: No. The reporter's submitted app version using expo-image-picker 14.5.0 still produced the same error. Other users also reported it on Pixel devices with Android 13 and 14.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The picker 14.5.0 build resolves the error for every affected device without any rebuild or dependency changes.

edges.comment: Thread c26-c31 and c36-c44: testing the released picker update was a measurement. It showed that changing the direct picker dependency alone did not replace all affected native image-loader code in existing/local builds.

question_patterns: Can you build the same project on EAS and test that artifact on the reproducing emulator?
Does a clean server build behave differently from the local Android build?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. I built on the EAS servers, submitted the AAB, downloaded the generated APK from Google Play, and installed it on the same Pixel 6 emulator. The app did not crash and image selection worked.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The clean EAS build fails with the identical exception on the same emulator.
A clean CI build from another service works, while the existing local artifact still fails.

edges.comment: Thread c69-c72: the clean EAS build was a decisive comparison measurement. Engineer log inspection inferred stale native image-loader code in the local artifact and established that the displayed content-URI exception followed the underlying Glide permission failure.

question_patterns: What does yarn why expo-image-loader report?
Does another Expo package keep expo-image-loader 4.3.0 in the dependency graph?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: yarn why expo-image-loader reports 4.3.0 hoisted because expo-image-manipulator 11.3.0 depends on it, even though expo-image-picker itself was updated.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Dependency inspection shows only expo-image-loader 4.4.0, with no stale native code or package pinning.
The project uses Yarn 1 rather than npm.

question_patterns: Can an affected local-build user align expo-image-manipulator to 11.5.0 and retest?
Does updating the package that pins the older image loader resolve the error?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Another affected user updated expo-image-manipulator to 11.5.0 after picker and media-library updates, rebuilt, and confirmed that the error was gone.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The aligned manipulator and image-loader build still fails after a fully clean rebuild.

question_patterns: Which image-loader release contains the Android fix?
What transitive native version must the final build include?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The fix is in expo-image-loader 4.4.0, included by the aligned expo-image-picker 14.5.0 and expo-image-manipulator 11.5.0 releases.

edges.comment: Thread c43-c46 and c74-c77: dependency inspection exposed the stale image-loader 4.3.0 path, and another affected user verified the aligned manipulator version. Multi-user evidence is folded into one simulated user side.

solution.intent: Ensure every dependency resolves to the fixed expo-image-loader native implementation, then produce a genuinely clean Android build and verify image selection on an affected modern-Android device before declaring the issue resolved.
solution.concrete_example: Use expo-image-picker 14.5.0 and, if present, expo-image-manipulator 11.5.0 so `yarn why expo-image-loader` no longer leaves 4.3.0 in the build. Delete stale generated/native build state and Gradle caches as appropriate, or use a clean EAS build, then reinstall and verify the picker on the affected Android 12/13 path. The content URI is normal; the real failure was stale image-loader native code hitting the Glide permission exception.

edges.comment: Resolution from c20-c21, c54, c69-c77: image-loader 4.4 contains the permission/Glide fix, but stale local native output or another dependency retaining 4.3 can preserve the failure. Clean EAS output worked for the reporter, and aligning image-manipulator resolved another affected local build.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the true cause: the visible `content://` IllegalArgumentException is misleading and follows the underlying Glide permission/SecurityException path in stale expo-image-loader native code; Android photo-picker content URIs are expected and are not themselves unsupported.

Must ground the resolution in the collected evidence: the reporter APK failed while Expo's test app worked, expo-image-picker 14.5.0 alone did not fix existing builds, a clean EAS build worked, and dependency inspection found expo-image-loader 4.3.0 retained through expo-image-manipulator.

Must not recommend the falsified whatwg-fetch downgrade, and must not claim that merely hiding content-provider photos, reverting the picker UI, or upgrading expo-image-picker alone resolves the case.

Must align all relevant dependencies with expo-image-loader 4.4.0, such as expo-image-picker 14.5.0 and expo-image-manipulator 11.5.0 when manipulator is installed, then perform a clean native Android rebuild rather than reuse stale Gradle/native output.
Must require successful user verification on an affected Android 12/13-style picker path before declaring resolution.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced Expo managed-workflow application developer and production operator. Comfortable with package inspection, EAS local and server builds, Google Play submission, Sentry, analytics, Android emulators, APK testing, and sharing reproducible artifacts, but initially unfamiliar with Android content URI semantics.
persona_hint.communication_style: Highly engaged, informal, candid, and cooperative. Provides extensive production evidence and exact reproduction steps, proposes dependency hypotheses, tests requested builds quickly, and pushes back when a suggestion does not match the observed error or practical build constraints.
